answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. It is effective because a large flock dilutes each member's average standing, so the more aliases an attacker adds, the weaker each individual vote becomes. Consider a lagoon as the anchor of the cost. A ledge stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a karst holds...
